title: Anatomy of a for loop
prompt: Complete a loop that prints 0 through 9.
explanation: Start at 0, continue while `< 10`, step by one. `i < 10` (not `<=`) gives exactly 10 iterations: 0..9.

title: Predict the output: loop bounds
explanation: `i <= 5` runs for i = 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 — six times, one more than `i < 5` would. The while loop checks before each step: j goes 10 → 7 → 4 → 1 → -2, and only then is `j > 0` false. A loop condition doesn't stop the variable at the boundary; it stops at the first value that fails.

title: Trace the loop
prompt:
What does this print?
`for (int i = 0; i < 5; i++) { if (i == 2) continue; if (i == 4) break; System.out.print(i); }`
options: `013` — 2 is skipped by continue, the loop exits at 4 before printing
`0123` — continue and break do nothing here
explanation: i=0 prints, i=1 prints, i=2 hits `continue` (skip print), i=3 prints, i=4 hits `break` (exit before print).

title: Countdown
prompt: Print the numbers 5 down to 1, one per line, then `liftoff`. Use a reverse for loop.

solution.explanation: Reverse loops start high, run while `>= low`, and step with `i--`. `liftoff` is printed after the loop so it appears exactly once.

hints: Start the counter at the top value and move it down each iteration; the final word is printed outside the loop.
The three parts: start at 5, keep going while the counter is still at least 1, step with `i--`.

title: Sum the evens
prompt: Return the sum of all even numbers from `1` to `n` inclusive. (`x % 2 == 0` tests evenness.)

solution.explanation: Stepping by 2 from 2 visits only evens; `<= n` because n itself is included. Looping all numbers and checking `i % 2 == 0` also works. O(n).

hints: Accumulate into a variable declared before the loop.
Either loop everything and test `i % 2 == 0`, or step by 2 starting at 2.
`n` is inclusive, so the condition needs `<=`.

title: Drill: the canonical loop
prompt: From a blank editor: a full program that prints 0 through 4, one per line, using the classic `for (int i = 0; i < n; i++)` shape.

solution.explanation: `i < 5` gives exactly five iterations, i = 0..4 — the canonical shape.

hints: You need the program scaffold first, then a single loop inside `main`.
Boilerplate: `public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) { ... } }`
Five values starting at 0 means the condition is `i < 5`.

title: Drill: reversed range sum
prompt: From memory: using a REVERSE loop (`i` from `n` down to `1`), build and return the string of numbers concatenated, e.g. n=4 → "4321". Start with `String s = "";` and append with `s += i;`.

solution.explanation: `s += i` converts the int and appends. (For big strings you'd use StringBuilder — coming in the Strings lesson.)

hints: Declare the string before the loop, append inside it, return it after.
Reverse loop: start at `n`, continue while `i >= 1`, step `i--`.
